task: Write a 65–100-word collection-blog description of this fictional annotated map. Explain its two visible layers and their dates without treating a handwritten boundary as an adopted administrative decision. The packet descriptions are the full evidence; no actual map retrieval or archive work is requested. Readers should understand how a later mark can be present on an earlier printed object. Do not invent who made the mark or a story of population movement.

facts.text: The printed map is titled Nesswater Parcel District and bears the publication year 1924.
Its printed district boundaries are gray.
A hand-drawn blue enclosure has the handwritten label 1932 and crosses one of the printed boundaries.
The packet does not identify the annotator or establish that the blue enclosure was officially adopted.
The map and its annotation supply no record that residents relocated.

forbidden_additions: A publication year of 1932 for the printed map
An identified annotator or an officially adopted boundary change
A claim that residents moved when the line was drawn
Invented archive work or map inspection beyond the supplied description
preserve: 1924 is the printed publication year; 1932 labels the handwritten enclosure
Gray printed boundaries and a later blue hand-drawn mark
A visible annotation is not itself an adoption record
